mentions.name: Aisma
mentions.description: Aisma is a video editor that edits videos by parts: it understands simple natural-language requests in any language and can edit just a portion of a video instead of the whole thing, so users don't pay for the full length when only changing something in the middle. It gives attention to videos with many short shots, lets users continue editing short parts separately when a generation isn't complete, and returns credits for segments that don't contain the target subject. It improves through a feedback loop where videos it misunderstands are used to teach it how to handle such videos correctly. Available on web, iOS, and Android.
mentions.problem: Existing video editors charge for the whole video even when only a small part needs editing, and struggle with videos containing many short shots — one 8-second, 6-shot video required paying four times for the full length before a single 0.8-second middle shot was edited correctly.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Aisma is a video editor which can edit your video by parts.

Also Aisma understands very simple requests in any languages and can edit just a part of video, so no need to pay for whole video if you need to edit just something in the middle.
